business_problem: Riley Children's Foundation had a 700,000-person donor prospect database but limited staff and predictive-modeling expertise, making it difficult for gift officers to identify and prioritize promising donor relationships efficiently.
solution_summary: Riley Children's Foundation uses Nonprofit Cloud to track donors and their cultivation lifecycle, then adds CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery to bring predictive insights into gift officers' workflow. CRM Analytics consolidates Salesforce and external data sources, and the team builds prospect-pool dashboards that show the donation pipeline and account context. Einstein Discovery's machine-learning model estimates the probability that a household will become a major-gift donor; embedded Salesforce dashboards expose those insights alongside donor interests, location, donation timing and supported programs. Gift officers use the context to prioritize cultivation and shape direct-mail and other outreach, while the analytics team avoids compiling data manually for each request. The source describes analytics and workflow integration but does not name the external data systems or model architecture.

Dashboards embedded in Salesforce surface account context and insights to gift officers, who use them to prioritize cultivation and donor outreach.

business_outcome: AI-driven donor insights help gift officers prioritize cultivation and spend less time finding data. The foundation is on track to reduce the donor cultivation lifecycle by 50% over the next two years and is working toward increasing donors giving $10,000 or more.

evidence_quotes: The team added CRM Analytics with Einstein Discovery to Nonprofit Cloud.

The new advanced analytics solution consolidated Salesforce data sources with external data sources, and empowered gift officers with AI-powered, actionable insights about their donors directly in their workflow with no coding required.
The team is on track to reduce the large donation cultivation lifecycle by 50% in the next two years.
